Casey.feeling: Round 3 feels tense and hard to read: I'm under pressure over the Owl rule, and the table has turned on me while Finley's death leaves the picture unclear.

Drew.feeling: Messy and frustrating: the Owl and egg-count stories keep contradicting each other, and Finley's early death left us with little to check.

Ellis.feeling: Round 3 is tense and messy: I'm Meowfia, I hid behind a Floofer claim, and the table is voting on Casey, so my cover feels fragile but still workable.

Finley.feeling: I'm dead and can't speak, and Ellis's Floofer claim looks like it hugged my Eagle visit, so the round feels like it's slipping toward a bad vote.

Alex.note: This is the last round, so my rule is to throw every card I hold. I'm throwing all 9 at Casey, who I think is the Meowfia.

Blair.note: Casey is the target. I'll throw two cards, the Wild and C6, to add votes against Casey without spending my high cards.

Casey.note: Ellis is my target. I'll throw both Wilds: they're worth 0 but still give two votes, and I keep my high cards.

Drew.note: Casey is the consensus target and the most likely Meowfia. I'll throw two cards at Casey to add votes, keeping my higher cards.

Ellis.note: Casey is the table's target and Casey's farm-side claims keep shifting, so throwing at Casey lines up with the vote. I'm throwing a low card and a mid card to add votes while keeping my higher cards.

Finley.note: I'm dead, so my throw doesn't count as a vote but still scores if Farm wins. Alex's Falcon claim conflicts with my Eagle count, which shows zero visitors on Alex besides me, so I'll throw at Alex with my lowest cards.

Alex.confusing: The Owl rule was the most confusing: several players disagreed on whether the Owl's egg goes to the Owl or the player they visit, and my confused Kookaburra report made my own egg count unreliable.
Alex.fun: Watching the table pile onto Blair in round 1 and then fight over Casey's visit story in round 2 was entertaining, especially the Owl-versus-Turkey egg-count arguments.
Alex.change: I'd make the dawn reports for confused players clearer about which numbers are wrong, so players can tell which claims to trust.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I threw all nine cards at Casey, who was Farm, instead of Ellis, the Floofer and a real Meowfia. I should have trusted Ellis's visit story less and checked the Floofer claim against Casey's dodge.

Blair.confusing: The Owl's dawn egg rule was muddled at the table, and several players thought the egg goes to the Owl rather than the visited player. Confused reports also made visit claims hard to check against nest counts.
Blair.fun: In Round 3, I Winked Finley and stayed hidden while the table spent the day chasing Casey's Owl story. Watching everyone argue over the Owl was satisfying.
Blair.change: Make dawn reports clearer about visitors and egg sources so players can check claims against nest counts without guessing the rules.
Blair.regret: In Round 2 I joined the caw and threw at Casey on thin evidence, and Casey was actually Farm. I would wait for firmer evidence and throw only low cards until the picture was clearer.

Casey.confusing: The Owl's egg rule was confusing at the table: "lay an egg in their nest" could mean the visited player or the Owl, and Drew and Alex argued the Owl's own nest. Dawn reports that don't list visitors also made it hard to check claims.
Casey.fun: Round 2 was the most fun: the Turkey, Tit and Kookaburra egg counts clashed, and the table had to work out who was lying from nest sizes alone.
Casey.change: I'd make dawn reports name the visitors whenever a role learns them, so claims like the Owl's are easy to check. I'd also make the Owl's egg rule explicit about whose nest gets the egg.
Casey.regret: In round 1 I voted with the table to throw at Blair, a Farm player, when Finley was the real Meowfia. I'd instead have questioned Finley's Hawk claim, since Finley visited Blair and was Meowfia, and thrown at Finley.

Drew.confusing: The Owl's egg rule was unclear: the egg seems to go to the Owl's own nest when nobody visits them, but the dawn reports and the table's claims about who gets the egg didn't line up. Casey's silence about visitors was hard to read.
Drew.fun: Watching Blair's Owl story collapse under three visits in round 1 and seeing the table vote it out was the most satisfying read of the game.
Drew.change: I'd make the dawn reports clearer about what each role learned, so players can check claims against the nest changes without guessing who is confused.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I threw at Casey, a Farm Owl, when Ellis, the Meowfia Floofer, was the one whose visit story didn't hold up; I should have pushed the vote toward Ellis.

Ellis.confusing: The Owl rule and the dawn reports were hard to track, since several players gave conflicting egg explanations and I couldn't tell which claims were honest. Roles also reshuffled every round, so the earlier claims were hard to check later.
Ellis.fun: My Tit guess of Pigeon on Casey paid an egg, which gave the table a verified anchor on the day. Watching Casey's shifting Turkey and Owl stories unravel was also satisfying to track.
Ellis.change: I'd make dawn reports name the visiting animals or give each player a clearer public record, so visit claims can be cross-checked without guesswork.
Ellis.regret: In round 1 I threw at Blair, the Owl, on the strength of three visit claims without testing Casey's and Finley's stories against each other. I'd question the visitors who were making the strongest claims before piling votes onto the player who looked least consistent.

Finley.confusing: The Owl and Kookaburra reports were hard to trust, and the rule that an Owl's egg goes to the player it visits versus its own nest was contested at the table. Nobody could settle it, so the day turned on it.
Finley.fun: Round 1 went well: my Hawk claim and the early vote on Blair got Blair eggsecuted and banked me 11 points. Watching the table build a case from nest counts was the best part.
Finley.change: Have the Storyteller state each Owl and Kookaburra visitor list and egg rule explicitly in the dawn report, so players aren't arguing over what the rules say.
Finley.regret: In round 2, as the Sphinx, I pushed the table to eggsecute Casey, a real Turkey, and backed Alex's suspicious +3 story was not the issue; I should have kept quiet and voted with the table instead of pushing a wrong target. I would have stayed quiet and kept my high cards.
